judgements.justification: A's AC restated its two 4s and B's AC followed four above-threshold scores; neither set the outcome from their own reading.
No reviewer or AC on either side rested the recommendation on a forecast of broad impact.
The 2021-09-03 thread cleared YbwL's additive-loss misreading and YbwL raised to 6 in B, while A got the same (1+ε) sketch and nobody moved.
Each committee had one weak review (A's K1Av partly inattentive, B's one-paragraph et4L 7); neither committee as a whole was thin.
Only A asked for a prediction-aware baseline and a closed-form ratio; A's meta-review counted the limited experiments against the paper, and no B reviewer questioned the ZCL-only design.

Both committees saw that guarantees hold only for correct predictions and robustness comes from the one-sentence γ-split; A's two confidence-4 reviewers rated 4 on it, while B's PbZr called robustness trivial and YbwL made it a revision item.
YbwL's raise came from the authors' clarification, not from other reviewers; no score moved on reviewer discussion.
No reviewer's rating plainly contradicts their own text; ZGPi's 6 with doubts is a borderline verdict, not a mismatch.
A's confidence-4 reviewers gave clear 4s on stated grounds, and B's 6s came at confidence 4; no committee defaulted to borderline scores from uncertainty.
Neither AC followed a single outlying reviewer; A's AC followed the two 4s, the majority.
The committees' written verdicts differ in substance (A: incomplete, misleading framing; B: technically strong), so the gap is weighting, not scale calibration.
B's AC cited 'technically strong and interesting', not reviewer agreement, and B held an 8, so the spotlight did not rest on unanimity alone.
YbwL raised on a correct clarification of the paper's own index, not on unverified new results.
B's short meta-review omits ZGPi's venue doubt but carries YbwL's additive-loss and incorrect-prediction points forward as revisions; it is not one-sided.
A's K1Av said robustness is not discussed, though lines 87-89 state a worst-case bound, and A's xbrn offered a boundary counterexample outside the continuous model; both fed A's 4s.
The authors' concession of no closed-form ratio did not raise or hold an inflated score; A rejected anyway.
No objection or score drop came after the author-response period.
The committees' scores differ (means 5.0 and 6.75), so the split does not come from different tier cut-offs on near-identical scores.
Neither AC passed over a better-informed reviewer: A followed its confidence-4 reviewers, and B's confidence-4 reviewers gave 6, inside the accept verdict.

B's main open concern was a misreading the authors could clear by clarification, while A's concerns (robustness trade-off, framing, prediction-aware baseline) needed new results that no response could supply.
No single score crossed a boundary: A's 7 did not lift a 4/4 committee, and B is above threshold without the 8.
A's outlying champion upZi was silent after the rebuttal, but its 7 was not a score the response had undercut; the silence is covered as a committee-wide pattern.
Neither AC set aside a detractor as unreliable.
Venue and motivation doubt came from both committees (A's K1Av, B's ZGPi), so it is not raised by one committee only.
A's meta-review statement that the paper does not address inaccurate predictions is accurate for the submission; B's misstates nothing.
No A reviewer posted or edited after the rebuttal, so the (1+ε) sketch and the γ-split pointer went unanswered, while B's YbwL and PbZr engaged and YbwL revised.
B's 8 (PbZr) and 7 (et4L) came at confidence 3 with math not carefully checked, while the two confidence-4 reviewers gave 6; the AC counted all four in full and reached a spotlight.
A's 7/4/4 is not an even split.
Both committees received the same (1+ε) sketch and the same γ-split pointer.
No novelty verdict rested on a wrong account of prior work.
B's three-sentence meta-review gives no reason for a spotlight over a poster with two 6s at confidence 4.
A's critics applied the learning-augmented standard that the paper's own introduction invokes, not a neighbouring field's premises.
A's champion upZi wrote a thorough five-hour review with 13 line comments, not a light one; the gap is post-rebuttal silence, covered by R26.
No committee rejected because promised fixes were too large.
Neither AC relied on assessments outside the record.

A held the paper to the consistency-robustness standard of learning-augmented algorithms and counted the missing trade-off against it, while B valued interval-prediction consistency on its own terms and called robustness trivial.

reasoning: The stage 1 verdict is that the committees weighted the same facts differently: robustness only via a one-sentence γ-split. A's confidence-4 reviewers held the paper to the learning-augmented consistency-robustness standard (R06, R36), with two checkable misreadings in A's critiques (R15) and an A-only baseline demand (R05). A stayed silent after the rebuttal while B engaged and YbwL raised on a clarification (R03, R20, R26). B's spotlight rests on unchecked confidence-3 scores and a meta-review with no tier argument (R27, R31). Each stage 1 candidate maps to an existing reason, so no reason is added.
